steps.text: Find shelter, stay dry, and cover all exposed skin.
steps.quote: Find Shelter: Try to stay dry and cover all exposed body parts.

steps.text: If no shelter is nearby, build a lean-to or windbreak for protection from the wind.
steps.quote: Build a lean-to, windbreak or snow cave for protection from the wind.

steps.text: Wear a wind- and waterproof jacket over warm insulating layers.
steps.quote: a wind and waterproof jacket will keep out wind, rain and wet snow

steps.text: Choose wool or synthetic clothing instead of cotton, which will not keep you warm when wet.
steps.quote: Choose clothing made of wool or synthetic material over cotton. Cotton absorbs moisture easily and won’t keep you warm if it gets wet.

steps.text: Keep your feet dry with wool socks, gaiters, and insulated boots.
steps.quote: Keep feet dry with wool socks, gaiters, and insulated boots.

steps.text: Set up your shelter in the shade.
steps.quote: Set up your tent in the shade

steps.text: Wear a wide-brimmed sun hat to shield your face and neck from direct sun.
steps.quote: Wear a wide brim sun hat to shield your face and neck from the sun as much as possible

steps.text: Avoid high-energy activity and outdoor work during midday heat if possible.
steps.quote: Avoid high-energy activities or outdoor work during midday heat if possible.

steps.text: Drink plenty of water, even if you do not feel thirsty.
steps.quote: Whether you feel thirsty or not, drink plenty of water

steps.text: Use a reflective sunshade to block strong sunlight.
Never ration drinking water unless authorities order it; drink what you need today and look for more for tomorrow.
steps.quote: Never ration drinking water unless ordered to do so by authorities. Drink the amount you need today and try to find more for tomorrow.

steps.text: Look for streams or rivers as possible water sources.
steps.quote: Streams, rivers, and other moving bodies of water

steps.text: Treat water collected from outside before drinking it.
steps.quote: Water from sources outside the home must be treated to kill harmful germs as described in Make Water Safe in an Emergency.

steps.text: Do not drink water suspected of fuel or toxic-chemical contamination; boiling will not make it safe.
steps.quote: If you suspect or know the water is contaminated with toxic chemicals or fuels, it cannot be made safe and you should not drink or bathe in this water.

steps.text: If water is cloudy, filter it through a clean cloth, paper towel, or coffee filter before treating.
steps.quote: If the water is cloudy, first filter it through a clean cloth, paper towel, or coffee filter.

steps.text: Boil clear water for one minute; above 6,500 feet, boil it for three minutes.
steps.quote: Bring clear water to a rolling boil for 1 minute (at elevations above 6,500 feet, boil for 3 minutes).
